name: Bath-shua
overview: Bath-shua is identified as a male figure described as the Canaanitess and the mother of Judah's first three sons. His unique attribute highlights his role within the early genealogies of Israel, specifically connected to the tribe of Judah. There is no additional tribal or personal information provided beyond this maternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Bath-shua means 'daughter of Shua,' indicating a familial lineage. This title is not given by God and serves primarily as a descriptive designation rather than a divine name. The reference for this name is found in 1 Chronicles 2:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Bath-shua as the mother of Er, Onan, and Shelah, Judah's first three sons. These relationships are inferred from 1 Chronicles 2:3. No further family connections are documented in the provided facts.
scriptureSignificance: Bath-shua's significance lies in her role as the mother of Judah's first three sons, establishing an important link in the Messianic lineage through the tribe of Judah. Her identity as a Canaanitess emphasizes the integration of non-Israelite individuals into God's providential plan, ultimately leading to the birth of Christ. This connection underscores God's sovereignty in working through diverse backgrounds to fulfill His redemptive purposes.
